headline: Forty US state attorneys general have asked the Character.AI bankruptcy court to make any buyer of its assets protect children and their private chats.
score_reason: Kept at pool score: bipartisan state action with a concrete court filing; the sale outcome is still open.
importance_line: Private chats of many young users could pass to a new owner, and the states want age checks, crisis safeguards and data deletion made conditions of any sale, though the judge has yet to rule.
summary: The Verge reports that 40 bipartisan attorneys general, including Letitia James, the attorney general of New York, filed a notice of interest in the bankruptcy case of the chatbot app Character.AI, citing its sensitive chats and the many minors who use it; Character.AI announced on 13 Oct that it was filing for Chapter 11 and selling some assets to Disney, a story we carried on 14 Oct. They want the judge to require the buyer to use effective age checks, limit how minors use the chatbots, add crisis safeguards and let users delete their data; several states had been investigating the company since 2024.
notes: Pool link (Reuters) was blocked; read The Verge, which reported on its own. Follows the bankruptcy story of our 14 Oct edition, but the AG filing is new.
